paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think this whole dinner is about: how you carry yourself when you're invited. Jesus heals a man on the Sabbath while the room stays silent. (Luke 14:3-4) Then, after He notices how the guests choose the places of honor, He says, "For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted." (Luke 14:7, 11) Grabbing the best seat gets you humbled, and the last seat is where the host may tell you to move up. (Luke 14:9-10)

Then Jesus tells the host to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind, people who "cannot repay you." (Luke 14:13-14) That is the heart of grace, friend. A gift that can't be paid back is a gift, and a host who gives like that "will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous." (Luke 14:14) When one guest says, "Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God," Jesus answers with a story about a banquet. (Luke 14:15-16)

In that story, the invited guests make excuses about a field, some oxen and a wife. Then the master tells his servant to bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame, and to go out to the highways and hedges so that his house will be full. (Luke 14:18-23) Excuses are easy, baker. The invitation is the thing to take seriously, because the servant says "everything is now ready." (Luke 14:17) So say yes to the invitation, take the last seat with a thankful heart, and let the Host decide who moves up.
